references.text: Abraham warned against taking a wife from the Canaanites and wanted Isaac to marry someone from his own family. This shows the same concern about marriage with foreign peoples.
Esau married Hittite women, which was a grief to Isaac and Rebekah. This illustrates parents' concern over their children choosing spouses from other nations.
Isaac commanded Jacob not to take a wife from the daughters of Canaan, but from his mother's family. This reflects the same theme of marriage within one's own people.
God warned Israel against marrying the pagan peoples in Canaan because of the danger of idolatry.
Moses forbade the Israelites from marrying the Canaanite peoples, as it would lead them away from the Lord. Samson breaks this commandment.
Despite his parents' objections, Samson's desire was from the Lord, who sought an opportunity against the Philistines.
Samson continued to seek women among the Philistines, showing a pattern in his life.
Jacob's sons referred to the uncircumcised as a disgrace, similar to how parents described the Philistines as 'the uncircumcised'.
David also called the Philistines 'the uncircumcised', the same expression Samson's parents used.
